content: PostgreSQL FUNCTIONS cannot COMMIT/ROLLBACK — always execute inside caller's transaction and any error rolls back all function-side effects atomically. PostgreSQL PROCEDURES (11+), invoked via CALL (not usable inside a SELECT/plain function body), CAN issue COMMIT/ROLLBACK, but only when called at the top level or via an uninterrupted CALL->CALL chain — control returns in a NEW transaction after COMMIT, so any state (e.g. temp table contents not ON COMMIT PRESERVE, or open cursors WITH HOLD needed) must be handled explicitly. This is a first-class design decision for translating Oracle procedures that COMMIT internally: they must become PG PROCEDURES, not FUNCTIONS, and cannot be called from inside another transaction-controlled function or from a query context.
